nodes.name: Install and webhook entry points
nodes.summary: Next.js App Router routes Saleor calls: manifest, register, two synchronous tax webhooks, two order webhooks, the order widget, the tRPC door and a cron job.
nodes.detail: Every route is a Next.js App Router handler composed with logger context, OpenTelemetry (OTel) metric flushing and span attributes. The manifest advertises four webhooks built from definition objects in src/modules/webhooks/definitions: CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES and ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES as synchronous webhooks, ORDER_CONFIRMED and ORDER_CANCELLED as asynchronous ones. The app SDK verifies the Saleor signature and loads the installation's auth data from the Auth Persistence Layer (APL) before a handler runs. Handlers read the app's encrypted configuration from the webhook payload's recipient private metadata, so a tax calculation needs no extra call back to Saleor.

nodes.name: Checkout and order tax calculation
nodes.summary: Turns a Saleor tax base into an AvaTax sales-order transaction, sends it, and maps the per-line result back into Saleor's synchronous webhook response.
nodes.detail: The checkout route uses CalculateTaxesUseCase; the order route still runs an older inline copy of the same steps. Both verify the payload has lines and an address, pick the AvaTax configuration for the channel, then build a CreateTransactionModel: document type is always SalesOrder so nothing is recorded, product lines get a tax code from the tax-class matches stored in metadata (default P0000000), shipping becomes a separate line with the configured shipping tax code, and subtotal discounts are sent as a document-level discount. The response transformer converts AvaTax lines into gross, net and integer tax rate per line, resetting the rate to 0 when the computed tax is 0 (exemptions). Results and errors are also written to the client log table.

nodes.name: Committing and voiding transactions
nodes.summary: On ORDER_CONFIRMED the app records the order in AvaTax as a sales invoice and saves the transaction code on the order; on ORDER_CANCELLED it voids that transaction.
nodes.detail: The confirmed-order route skips fulfilled orders and channels whose tax strategy is not the tax app (both answer 202), then builds a transaction with a document code (order metadata avataxDocumentCode or the order number, cut to 20 characters), a calculation date (metadata or order creation date) and SalesInvoice type when document recording is enabled. createOrAdjustTransaction makes the call idempotent. The returned AvaTax transaction code is written to the order's public metadata key avataxId and an order note is added after the response. The cancelled-order route reads avataxId through a metafield in its subscription and calls voidTransaction with reason DocVoided; a missing document maps to a dedicated error.

nodes.name: AvaTax API client
nodes.summary: A thin wrapper over the official avatax Node SDK that adds tracing, a request counter and error mapping for every call the app makes to Avalara.
nodes.detail: AvataxSdkClientFactory builds an Avatax SDK instance per configuration (sandbox or production, timeout from AVATAX_CLIENT_TIMEOUT, default 15000 ms) with the stored username and password. AvataxClient exposes createTransaction (really createOrAdjustTransaction), voidTransaction, validateAddress (resolveAddress), listTaxCodes, ping and getEntityUseCode, each traced as an OTel client span and counted in saleor.app.avatax.api.requests. A timeout message from the SDK becomes AvataxTimeoutError; everything else goes through AvataxErrorsParser, which maps Avalara fault codes such as InvalidAddress, GetTaxError, AuthenticationException and EntityNotFoundError to typed errors the routes branch on.

nodes.name: Configuration in Saleor app metadata
nodes.summary: Provider connections, channel assignments and tax-code matches, stored encrypted in the app's private metadata in Saleor and edited through tRPC routers.
nodes.detail: There is no app database for configuration. Three encrypted private metadata keys on the app hold JSON: tax-providers-v2 (AvaTax connections with credentials, company code, ship-from address and flags), channel-configuration (channel slug to connection id) and avatax-tax-code-map (Saleor tax class to AvaTax tax code). Webhook handlers decrypt them straight from the payload with getAppConfig, which tries the current SECRET_KEY and any rotation fallbacks. The dashboard edits them through tRPC routers that use CrudSettingsManager over the app SDK's EncryptedMetadataManager, fetching and mutating metadata through the Saleor GraphQL API with the app token. AppMetadataCache keeps the payload's metadata in AsyncLocalStorage for the request so nested reads skip a round trip.

nodes.name: Client logs in DynamoDB
nodes.summary: Per-installation logs of every tax calculation, commit and void, written to an Amazon DynamoDB table and browsable by staff in the app's logs page.
nodes.detail: Each webhook creates a DynamoDbLogWriter through LogWriterFactory. Log requests (calculate taxes, order confirmed, order cancelled) are validated with zod and written after the response with Next.js after(), in a detached trace. LogsRepositoryDynamodb writes every log twice in one batch write: one item keyed by date and one by checkout or order id, both under a partition key built from the Saleor API URL and app id, with a time to live (TTL) of DYNAMODB_LOGS_ITEM_TTL_IN_DAYS (default 14). The clientLogs tRPC router queries either view for the logs browser.

nodes.name: Runtime: auth storage, telemetry, problems
nodes.summary: Auth data storage in DynamoDB, environment validation, logging, Sentry and OTel set-up, app problem reports to Saleor and operational scripts.
nodes.detail: saleor-app.ts chooses the Auth Persistence Layer (APL): DynamoAPL on the main table when APL=dynamodb, otherwise a file. The DynamoDB client picks credentials from AWS_ROLE_ARN (Vercel OIDC) or access keys and sets request and connection timeouts (defaults 5000 and 2000 ms). The problem reporter turns recurring failures (invalid credentials, suspicious zero tax, missing channel configuration, invalid address) into Saleor app problems through the shared app-problems package. Scripts set up the DynamoDB tables, run webhook migrations and rotate the encryption key across installations.

nodes.name: Dashboard pages
nodes.summary: The React pages Saleor Dashboard shows inside its iframe: connection forms, channel table, tax-code matcher, logs browser and two dashboard widgets.
nodes.detail: Pages under src/pages use Macaw UI and call the tRPC routers through trpc-client with the dashboard-issued token. The configuration page lists provider connections and the channel table; providers/avatax pages create or edit a connection, validating credentials (ping) and the ship-from address (resolveAddress) before saving; the matcher page maps Saleor tax classes to AvaTax tax codes with a searchable combobox. order-details renders the transaction widget filled by POST /api/order-details; product-details shows which AvaTax tax code a product will use.

nodes.name: GraphQL documents, build and docs
nodes.summary: GraphQL fragments, subscriptions and mutations with their generated types, Bruno request collections, package and deployment configuration.
nodes.detail: graphql/ holds the subscription documents whose shape defines each webhook payload (TaxBase with metafields such as avataxEntityCode, avataxCustomerCode and avataxShipFromAddress), plus mutations for metadata, order notes and queries for channels and tax classes. graphql-codegen writes generated/graphql.ts. vercel.json schedules the stale-installation cron at 03:00 daily and pins regions dub1 and iad1.

nodes.name: GET /api/manifest
nodes.summary: Returns the AvaTax app manifest: permissions HANDLE_TAXES, MANAGE_ORDERS, MANAGE_PRODUCTS, the four webhooks and, from Saleor 3.22, two dashboard widgets.
nodes.detail: createManifestHandler builds the manifest from the request's base URL, overridable with APP_IFRAME_BASE_URL and APP_API_BASE_URL. Webhook entries come from appWebhooks, each definition producing its manifest with the subscription query. The order details widget posts to /api/order-details and the product widget loads /product-details. requiredSaleorVersion is >=3.22 <4.
nodes.signature: export const GET = compose(withLoggerContext, withFlushOtelMetrics, withSpanAttributesAppRouter)(handler)

nodes.name: POST /api/register
nodes.summary: Saleor's install call: exchanges the app token and stores auth data in the APL, refusing Saleor URLs that fail ALLOWED_DOMAIN_PATTERN.
nodes.detail: createAppRegisterHandler verifies the request, fetches the app id and stores saleorApiUrl, token and appId in the Auth Persistence Layer (APL). When ALLOWED_DOMAIN_PATTERN is set it is compiled as a regular expression and any non-matching Saleor URL is blocked and logged. A failed save is logged by onAplSetFailed.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/checkout-calculate-taxes
nodes.summary: Synchronous CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES webhook: runs CalculateTaxesUseCase and answers Saleor with per-line and shipping taxes, or a status code for each failure.
nodes.detail: The handler checks the subscription payload for GraphQL errors, extracts the app configuration from the recipient's private metadata (400 if broken), then calls CalculateTaxesUseCase. Success returns the sync webhook payload with status 200, optionally updating the checkout's avataxExemptionStatus public metadata after the response and reporting a suspicious zero-tax problem. Errors map to 504 (AvaTax timeout), 400 (address rejected by AvaTax), 202 (incomplete payload, expected), 500 (configuration broken, AvaTax error or unhandled), each with a span status and, where useful, an app problem.
facts: Incomplete payload answers 202 so Saleor does not treat it as a failure
Configuration is read twice: once in the route and again inside the use case

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/order-calculate-taxes
nodes.summary: Synchronous ORDER_CALCULATE_TAXES webhook for draft and unconfirmed orders; same steps as checkout but through a deprecated inline calculateTaxes function.
nodes.detail: The route keeps its own calculateTaxes function, marked deprecated in favour of CalculateTaxesUseCase, building the same payload service, transformer and adapter per request. It logs with sourceType order, updates exemption status metadata when enabled, and maps failures to status codes. Unlike the checkout route, several expected failures answer 202 rather than 4xx.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/order-confirmed
nodes.summary: Asynchronous ORDER_CONFIRMED webhook: commits the order to AvaTax, stores the transaction code in order metadata and adds an order note.
nodes.detail: Builds SaleorOrderConfirmedEvent from the payload; fulfilled orders and channels not using the tax app strategy are skipped with 202. With a valid channel configuration it calls the order-confirmed adapter, writes avataxId with OrderMetadataManager, then after the response writes a success log and an order note. Known AvaTax errors (bad payload, string length, entity not found, wrong user input, system error, invalid credentials, forbidden) map to 400 or 500 and may raise app problems.

nodes.name: POST /api/webhooks/order-cancelled
nodes.summary: Asynchronous ORDER_CANCELLED webhook: voids the AvaTax transaction whose code is in the order's avataxId metadata.
nodes.detail: Parses the payload into SaleorCancelledOrderEvent. Orders without avataxId answer 200 with an error log (nothing to void); broken or missing configuration answers 400. The adapter calls voidTransaction; a document AvaTax cannot find answers 202, an already cancelled transaction 200, credential and system errors may raise app problems, anything else 500.

nodes.name: POST /api/order-details
nodes.summary: Order details widget target: verifies the dashboard JSON Web Token (JWT), loads the order's AvaTax transaction and renders exemption and taxable totals.
nodes.detail: Reads orderId, saleorApiUrl, accessToken and appId from the form post and verifies the JSON Web Token (JWT). It queries the order's avataxId metafield and channel through GraphQL, finds the channel's provider connection with CrudSettingsManager, fetches the transaction with getTransactionByCode and caches it in an in-process Map keyed by API URL, app, order and transaction. It then fetches the app's own /order-details page with exemption number, total exempt and total taxable in the query string and returns that HTML.
facts: In-memory cache has no size limit or expiry
No avataxId answers 202 'AvaTax was not used for this order'

nodes.name: POST /api/trpc/{trpc}
nodes.summary: The typed remote procedure call (tRPC) door for the dashboard pages; also exported as GET for queries.
nodes.detail: fetchRequestHandler serves appRouter with createTrpcContext, which reads the Saleor API URL and the dashboard token from headers. Internal server errors are logged as errors, others at debug level.

nodes.name: GET /api/cron/cleanup-stale-installations
nodes.summary: Daily cron that removes APL records of installations whose Saleor instance no longer exists, guarded by CRON_SECRET.
nodes.detail: withCronAuthAppRouter checks the cron secret, then the shared cleanupStaleInstallations lists installations from the Auth Persistence Layer (APL), checks them against the Saleor Cloud API and deletes stale records from the DynamoDB main table, or only reports them when STALE_INSTALLATIONS_CLEANUP_DRY_RUN is set. maxDuration is 300 seconds.

nodes.name: Webhook list for the manifest
nodes.summary: Lists the four webhook definitions the manifest advertises and the migration script registers.

nodes.name: Webhook definitions
nodes.summary: SaleorSyncWebhook and SaleorAsyncWebhook objects binding each event to its subscription document and route path.
nodes.detail: Each definition names the event, the generated untyped subscription document (CalculateTaxes, OrderConfirmed, OrderCancelled) and the webhook path, and shares the app's APL so the SDK can verify signatures and load auth data.

nodes.name: Calculate-taxes payload check
nodes.summary: Rejects a tax base with no lines or no address as an expected incomplete payload.

nodes.name: Auth Persistence Layer choice
nodes.summary: Creates the SaleorApp with DynamoAPL on the main DynamoDB table when APL=dynamodb, otherwise a FileAPL.
nodes.detail: The Auth Persistence Layer (APL) stores each installation's Saleor API URL, app token and app id. With APL=dynamodb it uses DynamoAPL from the app SDK on dynamoMainTable and forwards its log messages; any other value falls back to FileAPL at FILE_APL_PATH, which only suits local development.

nodes.name: Calculate-taxes use case
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a checkout tax calculation: payload check, configuration lookup, AvaTax call, error mapping and client logging.
nodes.detail: Errors are typed subclasses the route switches on: ExpectedIncompletePayloadError, ConfigBrokenError, TimeoutError, InvalidAppAddressError, FailedCalculatingTaxesError and UnhandledError. Dependencies that need runtime values (the AvaTax client, tax-code matches service built from auth data) are created per call inside callAvaTax.

nodes.name: CalculateTaxesUseCase.calculateTaxes()
nodes.summary: Verifies the payload, finds the channel's AvaTax connection, calls AvaTax and logs success or failure to DynamoDB.
nodes.detail: Reads private metadata from payload.recipient and the channel slug from the tax base. If configuration extraction or channel lookup fails it writes an error log and returns ConfigBrokenError. Otherwise callAvaTax builds the SDK client, adapter and payload service and sends the transaction; rejections are mapped by type (timeout, invalid address, wrong user input treated as incomplete payload, anything else as FailedCalculatingTaxesError). Log entries always use sourceType checkout.
nodes.signature: async calculateTaxes(payload: CalculateTaxesPayload, authData: AuthData): Promise<Result<AvataxCalculateTaxesResult, CalculateTaxesUseCaseError>>

nodes.name: Unhandled tax error reporter
nodes.summary: Sends unexpected calculate-taxes failures to Sentry with the HTTP status the route returns.

nodes.name: Calculate-taxes adapter
nodes.summary: Sends the prepared transaction to AvaTax and transforms the answer; also defines the suspicious zero-tax line check.
nodes.detail: suspiciousLineCalculationCheck flags a line whose gross equals net while the rate is not zero and the line is not zero; routes use it to raise an app problem after responding.

nodes.name: AvataxCalculateTaxesAdapter.send()
nodes.summary: Logs a redacted view of the model, calls createTransaction, throws on error and returns both the raw transaction and Saleor's response shape.

nodes.name: Calculate-taxes payload service
nodes.summary: Loads the tax-class to tax-code matches from metadata, then asks the transformer for the AvaTax model.
nodes.detail: One GraphQL metadata read per calculation unless the request's metadata cache already holds the app metadata from the webhook payload.

nodes.name: Saleor tax base to AvaTax model
nodes.summary: Builds the CreateTransactionModel for a calculation: SalesOrder type, entity use code, customer code, company code, discount, addresses and lines.
nodes.detail: The document type is always SalesOrder, which AvaTax never records. The entity use code is checked against AvaTax with listEntityUseCodes. The customer code comes from checkout or order metadata, then the user's legacy metadata, then the user id, then 0. Ship-from uses the avataxShipFromAddress private metafield when valid, else the configured address; ship-to is the tax base address.

nodes.name: PayloadTransformer.transform()
nodes.summary: Assembles the AvaTax transaction model from the tax base, configuration, matches and discount strategy.
nodes.signature: async transform({ payload, avataxConfig, matches, discountsStrategy }): Promise<CreateTransactionArgs>

nodes.name: Tax base lines to AvaTax lines
nodes.summary: Maps each checkout or order line to an AvaTax line with its tax code, and adds a shipping line priced net of shipping discounts.
nodes.detail: Shipping discounts are summed and subtracted from the shipping price, floored at 0 with a Sentry report if Saleor sent more discount than price. Lines are marked discounted when subtotal discounts exist, so AvaTax spreads the document discount over them.

nodes.name: AvataxCalculateTaxesTaxCodeMatcher.match()
nodes.summary: Picks the AvaTax tax code for a line from its product's Saleor tax class, falling back to the default code.

nodes.name: AvaTax result to Saleor response
nodes.summary: Combines the shipping transformer and the lines transformer into Saleor's CalculateTaxesResponse.
nodes.detail: The shipping part finds the line with the shipping item code and reports shipping gross, net and rate; product lines are handled by the lines transformer.

nodes.name: ResponseLinesTransformer.transform()
nodes.summary: Turns each non-shipping AvaTax line into total gross, total net and an integer tax rate; non-taxable lines report rate 0.
nodes.detail: Gross is taxable amount plus tax calculated, rounded to 2 decimal places. When AvaTax returns a standard rate but zero tax (an exemption), the rate is reset to 0 so Saleor does not re-apply it. Missing numeric fields throw TaxBadPayloadError.

nodes.name: Discount strategies
nodes.summary: Two strategies: calculations send subtotal discounts as a document discount; order commits send none because prices already include reductions.
nodes.detail: AutomaticallyDistributedProductLinesDiscountsStrategy sums discounts of type SUBTOTAL and marks lines discounted when the sum is above 0. PriceReductionDiscountsStrategy, used on ORDER_CONFIRMED, returns undefined for both, leaving line prices as the discounted amounts.

nodes.name: Address mapping
nodes.summary: Converts Saleor addresses and the configured channel address into AvaTax address models.
nodes.detail: fromSaleorAddress maps street lines, city, country area, postal code and country code; fromChannelAddress maps the configured street, city, state, zip and country. AvaTax receives these as AddressLocationInfo for ship-from and ship-to.

nodes.name: Customer code resolver
nodes.summary: Chooses the AvaTax customer code: source metadata, then the user's legacy metadata, then the user id, then 0.

nodes.name: AvataxEntityTypeMatcher.match()
nodes.summary: Validates the avataxEntityCode metafield against AvaTax's entity use codes and returns it, or an empty string.
nodes.detail: The try block returns validateEntityCode's promise without awaiting it, so a rejection (an AvaTax error, or an empty result list where value?.[0].code dereferences undefined) escapes the catch and fails the whole calculation instead of falling back to an empty code.

nodes.name: Ship-from address resolver
nodes.summary: Parses the avataxShipFromAddress private metafield with zod and falls back to the configured address when missing or invalid.

nodes.name: Exemption status metadata writer
nodes.summary: After a calculation, updates or deletes the avataxExemptionStatus public metadata on the checkout or order when exemption data changed.
nodes.detail: A plan function compares the current metafield with the new exempt total, entity use code and time, and returns none, update or delete. ExemptionStatusMetadataManager runs the matching updateMetadata or deleteMetadata mutation; errors go to the caller's onError.

nodes.name: Tax error types
nodes.summary: Typed errors for AvaTax faults and incomplete payloads that routes and use cases branch on.
nodes.detail: Errors subclass the app's BaseError: AvataxTimeoutError, AvataxInvalidAddressError, AvataxGetTaxWrongUserInputError, AvataxGetTaxSystemError, AvataxInvalidCredentialsError, AvataxForbiddenAccessError, AvataxEntityNotFoundError, AvataxStringLengthError, TaxBadPayloadError and the incomplete-payload group. Routes switch on these classes to pick a status code and whether to raise an app problem.

nodes.name: Order-confirmed adapter factory
nodes.summary: Wires the SDK client, entity matcher, lines transformer, date and document code resolvers into an order-confirmed adapter for one configuration.

nodes.name: AvataxOrderConfirmedAdapter.send()
nodes.summary: Builds the order transaction model, calls createTransaction and returns the AvaTax transaction code.
nodes.signature: async send({ payload, config, authData, discountsStrategy }): Promise<CreateOrderResponse>

nodes.name: Order-confirmed payload service
nodes.summary: Loads tax-code matches with the installation's auth data and hands them to the order transformer.
nodes.detail: It builds an AvataxTaxCodeMatchesService from the installation's auth data, so the matches are read through GraphQL metadata (or the request cache), then calls the confirmed-order transformer.

nodes.name: Confirmed order to AvaTax model
nodes.summary: Builds the transaction to record: document code, SalesInvoice type when recording is on, date, customer code, addresses, lines and email.
nodes.detail: Ship-to is the order's shipping address, else its billing address, else TaxBadPayloadError. Ship-from is always the configured channel address: the OrderConfirmed subscription does not fetch the avataxShipFromAddress metafield that calculations honour, so a per-order ship-from used during calculation is not used when the order is recorded.

nodes.name: matchDocumentType()
nodes.summary: Records the order as SalesInvoice only when isDocumentRecordingEnabled; otherwise SalesOrder, which AvaTax does not record.

nodes.name: Order lines to AvaTax lines
nodes.summary: Maps confirmed order lines and shipping to AvaTax lines using the order tax-code matcher.
nodes.detail: Product lines carry amount (with or without tax depending on the channel's prices entered with tax), tax code from the order tax-code matcher, quantity, item code and description. When the order has shipping, a line with the shipping item code and the configured shipping tax code is appended.

nodes.name: Document code resolver
nodes.summary: Uses the avataxDocumentCode metafield or the order number as the AvaTax document code, cut to 20 characters.

nodes.name: Calculation date resolver
nodes.summary: Uses a valid ISO date in avataxTaxCalculationDate metadata, else the order creation date.

nodes.name: Confirmed order event
nodes.summary: Wraps the ORDER_CONFIRMED payload with accessors: isFulfilled, isStrategyTaxApp, addresses, metafields and lines.

nodes.name: Cancelled order event
nodes.summary: Parses the ORDER_CANCELLED payload and exposes the avataxId metafield and channel.

nodes.name: AvataxOrderCancelledAdapter.send()
nodes.summary: Voids the AvaTax transaction named by avataxId for the configured company; a missing document raises DocumentNotFoundError.
nodes.signature: async send({ payload, config }: { payload: CancelOrderPayload; config: AvataxConfig })

nodes.name: updateOrderMetadataWithExternalId()
nodes.summary: Writes the AvaTax transaction code to the order's public metadata key avataxId with the updateMetadata mutation.
nodes.detail: Marked deprecated in the code. The value is what ORDER_CANCELLED later voids and what the order widget looks up. A GraphQL or mutation error is thrown, which makes the confirmed-order route answer with an error after the AvaTax transaction already exists.

nodes.name: Order note reporter
nodes.summary: Adds a note such as 'Transaction confirmed in AvaTax: <code>' to the order with the orderNoteAdd mutation.

nodes.name: AvaTax client
nodes.summary: Traced, counted wrappers around the AvaTax SDK calls the app uses, returning neverthrow results.
nodes.detail: Each wrapped call sets peer.service avatax on its span and an avatax.enviroment attribute derived from the SDK base URL (sandbox when it is https://sandbox-rest.avatax.com). The tenant domain attribute is limited by OTEL_TENANT_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST.

nodes.name: AvataxClient.createTransaction()
nodes.summary: Calls createOrAdjustTransaction so a transaction created in an older flow can be committed idempotently.

nodes.name: AvataxClient.voidTransaction()
nodes.summary: Voids a transaction with reason DocVoided and logs the parsed error on failure.

nodes.name: AvataxClient.validateAddress()
nodes.summary: Resolves an address with AvaTax address validation, used before saving a connection's ship-from address.

nodes.name: AvaTax SDK client factory
nodes.summary: Creates an Avatax SDK instance for sandbox or production with the stored credentials and AVATAX_CLIENT_TIMEOUT.

nodes.name: AvaTax error parser
nodes.summary: Maps Avalara fault codes to typed errors and reports unknown shapes to Sentry.

nodes.name: Transaction details fetcher
nodes.summary: Fetches a committed transaction by code for the order details widget.

nodes.name: Credential obfuscator
nodes.summary: Masks AvaTax passwords before connections are sent to the dashboard, and detects masked values on edit.

nodes.name: AppConfig.getConfigForChannelSlug()
nodes.summary: Finds the channel's configuration and the AvaTax connection it points to; distinguishes an unknown channel from a deleted connection.

nodes.name: getAppConfig()
nodes.summary: Decrypts every private metadata entry with SECRET_KEY (and rotation fallbacks) and keeps the ones that parse as provider connections or channel configuration.
nodes.detail: Each value is decrypted and parsed as JSON, then tried against the provider connections schema and the channels schema. Entries matching neither, such as the tax-code map, are ignored. A missing SECRET_KEY throws.

nodes.name: Encrypted settings manager
nodes.summary: Creates the app SDK's EncryptedMetadataManager over the app's private metadata, reading through the request cache first.
nodes.detail: fetchMetadata returns cached metadata when the webhook already supplied it, else queries app.privateMetadata; mutateMetadata uses updatePrivateMetadata on the app id and deleteMetadata uses deletePrivateMetadata. Rotation fallback keys decrypt values written with an older key.

nodes.name: List-in-metadata store
nodes.summary: Treats one metadata key as a list of items with ids: read all, read by id, create, update and delete.

nodes.name: Provider connections
nodes.summary: Schema and router for the list of AvaTax connections, returned to the dashboard with passwords obfuscated.
nodes.detail: Connections are stored under the encrypted key tax-providers-v2. The router's getAll goes through PublicProviderConnectionsService and PublicAvataxConnectionService, which obfuscates credentials before they reach the dashboard.

nodes.name: AvaTax connection schema
nodes.summary: zod schema for one connection: name, sandbox flag, credentials, company code, autocommit, document recording, shipping tax code, address and exemption flag.

nodes.name: AvaTax connection router
nodes.summary: tRPC procedures to list, read, create, update and delete connections and to validate credentials and addresses against AvaTax.
nodes.detail: Create and update call AvataxConnectionService, which pings AvaTax before saving. Separate edit procedures exist because the edit form holds obfuscated credentials; AvataxPatchInputTransformer merges the stored secret back before validating.

nodes.name: Address validation service
nodes.summary: Formats the connection's ship-from address and resolves it with AvaTax before the connection is saved.

nodes.name: Channel configuration router
nodes.summary: tRPC procedures that list Saleor channels with their assigned connection and upsert an assignment.
nodes.detail: The service merges channels fetched from Saleor with the channel-configuration metadata list, so channels without an entry appear unassigned.

nodes.name: Tax-code matches
nodes.summary: Reads and upserts the Saleor tax class to AvaTax tax code map stored under avatax-tax-code-map.

nodes.name: AvaTax tax-code search
nodes.summary: Lists AvaTax tax codes filtered by text for the matcher combobox.

nodes.name: Saleor tax classes
nodes.summary: Fetches the store's tax classes from Saleor for the matcher page (first 100 only).
nodes.detail: The fetcher runs the TaxClassesList query with first set to 100 and no pagination (a todo in the code), so stores with more tax classes see only the first 100 in the matcher. The router exposes them to the matcher page.

nodes.name: tRPC server and auth
nodes.summary: Router assembly, context and the protected procedure that verifies the dashboard JSON Web Token (JWT) and loads the app token from the APL.
nodes.detail: protectedClientProcedure looks up auth data for the Saleor API URL header, verifies the dashboard token with verifyJWT against the app id and required permissions, and puts a GraphQL client with the app token in context. trpc-app-router guards against being imported in the browser because it pulls in Node-only modules.

nodes.name: DynamoDB log writer
nodes.summary: Defers each log write until after the response with afterDetached, so webhook latency is unaffected.

nodes.name: Log writer factory
nodes.summary: Creates a DynamoDB client, logs table, repository and writer for every call; there is no feature switch to the no-op writer.

nodes.name: Logs repository
nodes.summary: Writes each log by date and by checkout or order id in one BatchWrite, and queries either view with pagination.
nodes.detail: Unprocessed batch items are detected and reported as an error. Reads use QueryCommand on the date or id entity, mapping items back with the log transformer.

nodes.name: Logs table and entities
nodes.summary: dynamodb-toolbox table with PK and SK keys and two entities, LOG_BY_DATE and LOG_BY_CHECKOUT_OR_ORDER_ID, each with a TTL attribute.

nodes.name: Log entry model and requests
nodes.summary: Client log shape plus builders for calculate-taxes, order-confirmed and order-cancelled success and error entries.
nodes.detail: Each request builder validates its input with zod and returns a neverthrow result; callers log the error to Sentry or pass the entry to the log writer. Entries record source id and type, channel, event, success or error reason and, for calculations, the result.

nodes.name: Client logs router
nodes.summary: tRPC queries that page through logs by date range or by checkout or order id for the logs page.
nodes.detail: Two queries, getByDate and getByCheckoutOrOrderId, run on a procedure that builds the DynamoDB logs repository per request. Both validate their parameters with zod and return a page of logs with a cursor for the next page.

nodes.name: DynamoDB client and main table
nodes.summary: Builds the AWS DynamoDB document client and the main table (PK, SK) that holds APL auth records.
nodes.detail: Credentials come from AWS_ROLE_ARN through the Vercel OIDC provider, or from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY; region from AWS_REGION. Request and connection timeouts come from DYNAMODB_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS and DYNAMODB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS.

nodes.name: Environment schema
nodes.summary: Validates environment variables with zod: APL, SECRET_KEY, DynamoDB tables, AvaTax client settings, telemetry and cron settings.

nodes.detail: Keys include invalid credentials, forbidden access, company inactive or not found, entity not found, suspicious zero tax, tax-code permission, channel configuration missing and invalid address. Most use a critical threshold of 1.

nodes.name: Install and webhook entry points
nodes.summary: Next.js routes Saleor calls: manifest, register, the notify webhook, eight order, invoice and gift card webhooks, app-deleted, tRPC and two cron jobs.
nodes.detail: The app is marked deprecated in its manifest (replaced by a newer Customer Emails app) and its manifest declares only the APP_DELETED webhook. The event webhooks are created on the fly with webhookCreate when a configuration activates an event (and for every event at install when the Saleor Cloud fallback sender is configured). Each event route is a Pages Router handler built from SaleorAsyncWebhook with its own GraphQL subscription; NOTIFY_USER uses Saleor's legacy JSON payload instead of a subscription. Every handler finds the recipient email, then calls SendEventMessagesUseCase and maps its result to 200, 202, 400, 500 or 503.

nodes.name: Rendering and sending email
nodes.summary: For each active configuration that serves the channel and event: Handlebars renders subject and body, MJML turns the body into HTML, a plain-text copy is made, and nodemailer sends it.
nodes.detail: SendEventMessagesUseCase loads active configurations available in the channel. For each it checks the event's settings exist and are active and that a sender name and email are set, enriches the payload with branding and custom variables, compiles with EmailCompiler and sends with SmtpEmailSender, all in parallel. With no configuration it can fall back to a Saleor Cloud sender configured by FALLBACK_SMTP_* variables: the message goes to the organisation owner's address fetched from a redirect endpoint, with a banner and the original recipient in the subject. Errors are typed as retryable server, server, client or no-op errors.

nodes.name: Configuration per channel and event
nodes.summary: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) configurations, each with server, sender, branding, channel rules and per-event templates, stored encrypted in the app's private metadata.
nodes.detail: All configurations live in one encrypted private metadata key, smtp-config, read through the shared EncryptedMetadataManagerFactory with a 3000 ms timeout. A configuration holds host, port, encryption (NONE, TLS for STARTTLS, SSL), optional user and password, sender name and email, branding, custom variables, channel rules (override with restrict or exclude list) and one entry per event with active flag, subject and MJML template. The dashboard edits them through tRPC procedures; procedures flagged updateWebhooks re-sync Saleor webhooks afterwards.

nodes.name: Webhook management
nodes.summary: Keeps the Saleor webhooks registered for the app in line with which events are active in any configuration.
nodes.detail: syncWebhookStatus compares the current webhooks (by name, via the app's webhooks query) with the set implied by active configurations and creates or deletes the difference. createWebhook builds the target URL and subscription from the definition's manifest; for Saleor before 3.23 it strips the GiftCardPaymentMethodDetails fragment, decided by a feature flag service that reads Saleor's version.

nodes.name: Runtime: auth storage, telemetry, deprecation
nodes.summary: APL selection (DynamoDB, Upstash or file), environment schemas, logging, Sentry and OTel, the deprecation notice and maintenance scripts.
nodes.detail: saleor-app.ts builds the Auth Persistence Layer (APL) from the APL variable: dynamodb uses DynamoAPL on the main table described by env-dynamodb, upstash and file are also accepted, anything else throws at start. DynamoDB holds only installation auth data; configurations stay in Saleor metadata. A daily cron marks installations deprecated through the shared app-deprecation package.

nodes.detail: Used by the SMTP app and its preview script (and by the products feed app outside this area). nodes.name: Notify event mapping
nodes.summary: Maps Saleor notify_event names (account confirmation, password reset, email change, account delete, fulfillment update) to the app's event types.

nodes.name: Use-case error to HTTP status
nodes.summary: Looks at the first error only: retryable server errors answer 503, other server and client errors 400, no-op errors 200 and anything unrecognised 500, each with a safe message.
nodes.detail: Because only errors[0] decides the status, a mix of one sent and one failed configuration is reported as a failure even though one email went out; SMTP send failures answer 400 on purpose so Saleor does not retry and send duplicates.

nodes.name: Example event payloads
nodes.summary: Sample payloads per event used for template previews and the email preview build script.

nodes.name: Send-event-messages use case
nodes.summary: Sends one event's email through every matching configuration, or through the Saleor Cloud fallback sender when none match.
nodes.detail: Error classes encode retry policy: RetryableServerError (configuration fetch failed, redirect email fetch failed) is safe for Saleor to retry because nothing was sent; ServerError (SMTP failure) is not; ClientError covers template compilation, missing sender and token rejection; NoOpError covers disabled or missing event settings and an unconfigured fallback.

nodes.name: SendEventMessagesUseCase.sendEventMessages()
nodes.summary: Fetches active configurations for the channel, falls back when there are none, otherwise processes each in parallel and combines all errors.
nodes.signature: async sendEventMessages({ event, payload, recipientEmail, channelSlug, saleorApiUrl })

nodes.name: processSingleConfiguration()
nodes.summary: Checks the event is configured and active and the sender is set, enriches the payload, compiles the email and sends it with the configuration's SMTP settings.
nodes.detail: An SMTP response code 554 (message rejected) becomes a ClientError; every other send failure is a ServerError. User and password are only attached when smtpUser is set.

nodes.name: sendWithFallback()
nodes.summary: Saleor Cloud fallback: when enabled and FALLBACK_SMTP_* is set, sends the default template to the organisation owner's address with an X-SES-TENANT header.
nodes.detail: The sender address is derived from the Saleor API URL and FALLBACK_SMTP_SENDER_DOMAIN; the real recipient is replaced by the owner email fetched from FALLBACK_SMTP_EMAIL_REDIRECT_ENDPOINT, and the subject is prefixed with the original recipient.

nodes.name: Use-case factory
nodes.summary: Builds the use case per request from auth data: GraphQL client, metadata-backed configuration service, email compiler and SMTP sender.

nodes.name: Email compiler
nodes.summary: Compiles subject and body with Handlebars, the body with MJML, then derives plain text; also validates templates without sending.
nodes.detail: Every failure carries an error context (SUBJECT, BODY_TEMPLATE, BODY_MJML), a public message and a template error code so the editor can point at the problem. Empty subject or body after rendering are errors.

nodes.name: EmailCompiler.compile()
nodes.summary: Returns from, to, subject, HTML and plain-text body for one email, or the first compilation error.

nodes.name: Handlebars compiler
nodes.summary: Compiles a template with the payload using Handlebars plus the allow-listed helpers, classifying missing-helper and parse errors.

nodes.name: MJML compiler
nodes.summary: Converts Mailjet Markup Language (MJML) to HTML and treats any MJML validation error as a compile failure.

nodes.name: HTML to text
nodes.summary: Produces the plain-text alternative of the rendered email.

nodes.name: SmtpEmailSender.sendEmailWithSmtp()
nodes.summary: Creates a nodemailer transport for the configured encryption and sends the email, failing after 4000 ms.
nodes.detail: TLS means STARTTLS on a plain connection (secure false), SSL means an implicit TLS connection (secure true); both require at least TLSv1.3. NONE sends without TLS. A new transport is created per email.
facts: TLS minimum version TLSv1.3 for TLS and SSL modes

nodes.name: Payload enrichment
nodes.summary: Adds branding (site name, logo URL) and custom variables from the configuration to the template payload, for sending and previews alike.

nodes.name: Default templates
nodes.summary: Default MJML bodies and subjects for every event, used for new configurations and the fallback sender.

nodes.name: Saleor Cloud fallback helpers
nodes.summary: Derives the fallback sender address and tenant name from the Saleor API URL, builds the redirect endpoint URL and fetches the owner email.
nodes.detail: fetchRedirectEmail calls the redirect endpoint with an Authorization token header and validates organization.owner_email with zod; network, status and parse errors become RedirectEmailFetchError, which the use case treats as retryable.

nodes.summary: Package manifest, lint, test and TypeScript configuration and changelog of @saleor/handlebars.

nodes.name: SMTP configuration service
nodes.summary: Reads, filters and updates configurations held in the smtp-config metadata key, and the fallback-enabled flag.
nodes.detail: getConfigurations accepts filters for active state and channel availability (isAvailableInChannel). A rejected app token is surfaced as AppTokenRejectedError so the webhook does not retry a broken installation. Template updates are validated with the email compiler before saving.

nodes.name: SMTP metadata manager

nodes.summary: tRPC procedures to create, read, update and delete configurations and their sections, render template previews and manage the fallback flag.
nodes.detail: Mutations that can change which events are active carry meta updateWebhooks, so the procedure middleware re-syncs Saleor webhooks after they succeed. renderTemplate parses the payload JSON, enriches it and runs the email compiler, returning HTML or a coded error.

nodes.name: Channel availability rule
nodes.summary: A configuration serves every channel unless override is on; then restrict mode serves only listed channels and exclude mode all but listed ones.
nodes.detail: The comment above the function says a configuration is available when the assigned list is empty, but in restrict mode an empty list makes it available in no channel.

nodes.name: App configuration router

nodes.name: tRPC server and auth
nodes.summary: Router assembly, context, JSON Web Token (JWT) protected procedure and the procedure that injects the configuration service and re-syncs webhooks.
nodes.detail: protectedClientProcedure verifies the dashboard JSON Web Token (JWT) and loads the app token from the Auth Persistence Layer (APL). protectedWithConfigurationServices adds an SmtpConfigurationService to the context and, when a procedure's meta has updateWebhooks, runs syncWebhookStatus after the procedure succeeds.

nodes.name: Webhook management service
nodes.summary: Lists the app's webhooks, reports which event webhooks are active, and creates or deletes one by name.
nodes.detail: eventToWebhookMapping sends all six account events and ORDER_FULFILLMENT_UPDATE to the single notify webhook, and every other event to its own webhook.

nodes.name: syncWebhookStatus()
nodes.summary: Compares registered webhooks with those active configurations need, then creates the missing ones and deletes the unneeded ones in parallel.

nodes.name: Webhook GraphQL operations
nodes.summary: The app webhooks query and the webhookCreate and webhookDelete mutations.
nodes.detail: fetchAppWebhooks queries the app's webhooks (id, name, isActive, events); createAppWebhook and deleteAppWebhook run webhookCreate and webhookDelete and throw on GraphQL or mutation errors.

nodes.name: Feature flags by Saleor version
nodes.summary: Reads Saleor's version once per service and enables giftCardPaymentMethodDetails for Saleor 3.23 and newer.
nodes.detail: FeatureFlagService fetches Saleor's version with the shop query once and caches the resulting flags. The only flag, giftCardPaymentMethodDetails, is true for Saleor 3.23 and newer and decides whether webhook subscriptions may keep the GiftCardPaymentMethodDetails fragment.

nodes.name: Auth Persistence Layer choice
nodes.summary: Creates the SaleorApp with DynamoAPL, UpstashAPL or FileAPL from the APL variable and exports the supported Saleor range >=3.22 <3.24.
nodes.detail: With APL=dynamodb the DynamoDB settings are parsed from env-dynamodb (table name, region, timeouts, credentials) and the main table is created for DynamoAPL. upstash and file use the app SDK's UpstashAPL and FileAPL; any other value throws when the module loads.

nodes.summary: Creates the DynamoDB document client and the main table used by DynamoAPL for installation auth data.
nodes.detail: The client takes credentials from AWS_ROLE_ARN or access keys and sets request and connection timeouts (defaults 5000 and 2000 ms); the main table uses PK and SK string keys.

nodes.summary: Validates environment variables: APL, SECRET_KEY, base URLs, cron secret, deprecation cron settings and the FALLBACK_SMTP_* sender.

nodes.summary: Architecture notes for coding agents and developers; they say configurations are stored in DynamoDB or the APL, while the code keeps them in Saleor app metadata.

nodes.summary: Dependencies (mjml, handlebars, nodemailer, app SDK, tRPC), scripts, Docker Compose for local DynamoDB and lint, test and TypeScript settings.

nodes.name: Install and webhook entry points
nodes.summary: Next.js routes Saleor and the dashboard call: manifest, register, fourteen catalog webhooks, app-deleted, setup-indices, webhooks-status, tRPC and a cleanup cron.
nodes.detail: The manifest declares fourteen asynchronous webhooks (product, variant, stock, category and page events) plus APP_DELETED. All catalog webhooks are created inactive and only switched on with webhookUpdate once valid Algolia credentials are saved. Every catalog handler builds a webhook context (configuration from metadata, channels from GraphQL, an AlgoliaSearchProvider), performs one index operation and maps Algolia failures: record too large answers 413 and raises an app problem, invalid credentials answer 401 and deactivate the app, an unknown Algolia application id answers 401, other Algolia errors pass through their status, and a context failure answers 400.

nodes.name: Algolia indexing
nodes.summary: Turns Saleor products, variants, categories and pages into Algolia records and saves, deletes or configures them in per-channel indices.
nodes.detail: Each variant listed in a channel becomes one record in the index <prefix>.<channel slug>.<currency>.products, with objectID <productId>_<variantId>, only when the product's channel listing is visibleInListings. Records carry names, SKU, attributes, media, description as JSON and plain text, category hierarchy for hierarchical facets, prices, metadata and stock, filtered to the fields enabled in configuration. Stock comes from a separate channel-scoped GraphQL query because webhook payloads have no channel context. After saving, the variant is deleted from every other channel index so delisted variants disappear. Categories and pages go to one index each.

nodes.name: Configuration and webhook activation
nodes.summary: Algolia credentials, index prefix, enabled fields and page-type filter, stored encrypted in the app's private metadata and edited through tRPC.
nodes.detail: One encrypted metadata key, app-config-v2, holds the whole AppConfig; when it is empty, getConfig falls back to legacy per-domain keys (secretKey, appId, indexNamePrefix) and returns them without writing them back. Saving credentials first verifies them with Algolia getApiKey, then stores them, then enables the app's own webhooks and clears earlier authentication problems. The Admin API key is returned to the dashboard because bulk imports run in the browser.

nodes.name: Bulk import from the dashboard
nodes.summary: Browser-side import that pages through every product, category and page with the dashboard token and uploads them to Algolia in batches.
nodes.detail: The import card builds an AlgoliaSearchProvider in the browser from the configuration returned by tRPC, queries Saleor GraphQL directly with the dashboard token (products per channel, categories, pages) and calls updatedBatchProducts, updatedBatchCategories or updatedBatchPages per page of results, showing progress.

nodes.name: Runtime: auth storage, telemetry, problems

nodes.detail: The Auth Persistence Layer (APL) is DynamoDB, Upstash or a file depending on APL; only installation auth data goes to DynamoDB. The problem reporter raises app problems for invalid credentials, oversized records and failed index set-up, and deactivates the app on authentication failures. Traced effects time Saleor and Algolia calls with slow thresholds.

The handler loads configuration and channels in parallel, answers 400 when Algolia is not configured, and on failure reports an app problem (or deactivates the app on an authentication error) and answers 500. Non-POST requests get 405.

nodes.name: createWebhookContext()
nodes.summary: Loads the Algolia configuration from metadata and the channel list from Saleor, then builds the AlgoliaSearchProvider every handler uses.
nodes.detail: The channels query runs before the configuration check, so an unconfigured installation still costs a GraphQL call per webhook. A missing appConfig throws AppNotConfiguredError, which the handlers turn into a 400.
nodes.signature: export const createWebhookContext = async ({ authData }: { authData: AuthData })

nodes.name: Webhook error mapping
nodes.summary: Turns Algolia errors into their HTTP status, unknown Algolia application ids into 401 with deactivation, and context failures into 400.
nodes.detail: handleAlgoliaWebhookError answers with Algolia's status code and message when the error carries one, else 500. handleInvalidAppIdError reports the unknown application id, deactivates the app and answers 401. handleWebhookContextError answers 400 with the error message.

nodes.name: Webhook payload types
nodes.summary: TypeScript types of each catalog webhook payload.

nodes.name: Algolia search provider
nodes.summary: Implements the SearchProvider interface over algoliasearch: save, delete and batch operations per index, and index settings.
nodes.detail: Index names are computed from the channel list at construction. saveObjects, deleteObjects, deleteBy and setSettings are each wrapped in traced effects and use NEXT_PUBLIC_ALGOLIA_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5000 ms). Known Algolia errors are rethrown for the handlers to classify. The same class runs on the server for webhooks and in the browser for bulk import.

nodes.name: AlgoliaSearchProvider.updateProduct()
nodes.summary: Fetches channel stock for all the product's variants, then saves each variant; products with no variants are skipped.
nodes.detail: Variants removed from the product are not deleted here; that relies on PRODUCT_VARIANT_DELETED.

nodes.name: AlgoliaSearchProvider.#saveProductVariant()
nodes.summary: Saves the variant's record to each visible channel index, then deletes its objectID from every other channel index.
nodes.detail: The guard if (staleIndices) tests an array, which is always truthy, so a delete call is issued even when there is nothing stale (an empty batch).

nodes.name: AlgoliaSearchProvider.updateIndicesSettings()
nodes.summary: Sets searchable attributes and facets on every product index and on the category and page indices.

nodes.name: productAndVariantToAlgolia()
nodes.summary: Builds one Algolia record for a variant in a channel: names, SKU, attributes, media, description, category tree, prices, stock and metadata, then keeps only enabled fields.
nodes.detail: Attributes from product and variant are flattened into a record keyed by attribute name, with booleans and numbers typed. inStock is true when inventory is not tracked, else whether the channel-scoped quantity is positive. Description is stored both as parsed EditorJS JSON and as plain text. A comment marked BUG in the code notes that variant pricing is null in webhook payloads (no channel context), so webhook updates empty the pricing fields that a bulk import filled.

nodes.name: channelListingToAlgoliaIndexId()
nodes.summary: Names a channel's product index <prefix>.<channel slug>.<currency>.products, dropping an empty prefix.

nodes.name: Category and page records

nodes.detail: Categories are saved to one categories index under the prefix and pages to one pages index. Page records always carry title, slug, page type id and SEO title; plain-text content, SEO description, metadata and attributes are added only when enabled. The page-type filter is applied in the page webhook routes, not here.

nodes.name: Algolia error parser

flows.name: A checkout asks the AvaTax app for taxes
flows.summary: How Saleor's synchronous CHECKOUT_CALCULATE_TAXES webhook becomes an AvaTax sales-order transaction and comes back as per-line taxes.

steps.text: When checkout prices have expired, Saleor recalculates them. For a channel whose tax strategy points at the AvaTax app, it needs taxes from the app before it can answer the storefront.
Saleor renders the CalculateTaxes subscription (tax base, lines, addresses, metafields and the app's private metadata) and posts it synchronously, waiting for the answer.
The app SDK verifies the signature and loads the installation's token from the Auth Persistence Layer (APL). The route checks the payload for subscription errors and starts the use case.
The use case rejects a tax base without lines or address as an expected incomplete payload (answered 202).
Configuration comes from the webhook payload itself: each encrypted private metadata entry is decrypted with SECRET_KEY and parsed as provider connections or channel configuration.
The channel slug selects the AvaTax connection: credentials, company code, ship-from address and flags. An unknown channel or deleted connection ends in a configuration error and an app problem.
The tax base becomes a SalesOrder transaction (never recorded): entity use code checked with AvaTax, customer code from metadata, ship-from and ship-to addresses, subtotal discount and currency.
Each line gets the AvaTax tax code mapped to its product's Saleor tax class, or the default code; shipping becomes its own line with the configured shipping tax code.
The client calls createOrAdjustTransaction through the AvaTax SDK, traced and counted, with a 15 second default timeout.
AvaTax computes tax per line and returns the transaction model with taxable amounts, tax and rate details.
Each AvaTax line becomes gross, net and an integer rate; a zero tax with a non-zero rate (an exemption) is reported as rate 0.
A success or error entry is written to the DynamoDB logs table after the response, so staff can inspect it in the logs page.

The route answers 200 with the sync webhook payload. After responding it may update the checkout's exemption status metadata and report suspicious zero-tax lines; failures answer 504, 400, 202 or 500 by type.

flows.name: An order confirmation email is rendered and sent
flows.summary: How ORDER_CONFIRMED reaches the SMTP app and becomes an email rendered from MJML and Handlebars and sent through the store's mail server.

steps.text: Staff confirm an unconfirmed order (orders from checkout can also be confirmed automatically).
The webhook plugin finds apps subscribed to ORDER_CONFIRMED; for the SMTP app that webhook only exists because a configuration has the event active.
Saleor delivers the OrderConfirmed subscription payload (order details, lines, addresses, user email) asynchronously.
The handler takes the order's email (or the user's), answering 202 when there is none, and creates the use case from the installation's auth data.
Active SMTP configurations are loaded from the encrypted smtp-config metadata (3 second timeout) and filtered to those serving the order's channel.
Channel rules: no override serves all channels; restrict serves listed ones; exclude serves the rest.
For each configuration the ORDER_CONFIRMED settings must exist and be active and a sender must be set; branding and custom variables are added to the payload.
The subject and body templates are rendered with Handlebars, the body is compiled from MJML to HTML and a plain-text copy is derived.
Only allow-listed handlebars-helpers are available to templates, so staff-written templates cannot reach unsafe helpers.
Any MJML validation error stops the email and is reported as a template error.
nodemailer opens a connection with the configured encryption (STARTTLS, implicit TLS or none) and sends, failing after 4 seconds.
The store's own mail server accepts the message for delivery to the shopper.
Success answers 200. Failures answer 503 only when nothing was sent and a retry is safe, otherwise 400 so Saleor does not resend duplicates.

flows.name: A product update reaches the search index
flows.summary: How PRODUCT_UPDATED makes the Search app rewrite one Algolia record per variant and channel.

steps.text: Staff edit a product in the dashboard.
Saleor queues PRODUCT_UPDATED for subscribed apps; the Search app's webhook is active only after valid Algolia credentials were saved.
The ProductUpdated subscription payload (product, variants, channel listings, attributes, media, category) is posted asynchronously.
The handler checks the payload has a product and builds the webhook context.
The context reads the Algolia configuration from encrypted app metadata and the channel list from Saleor, then builds an AlgoliaSearchProvider with the index prefix and enabled fields.
Two calls back to the Saleor GraphQL API with the app token: app metadata and channels (and later variant stock).
updateProduct skips products without variants and fetches channel-scoped stock for all variants.
Stock is queried per channel because the webhook payload resolves quantityAvailable without a channel.
Each variant is grouped by the channel indices where the product is visible in listings.
One record per variant and channel: objectID productId_variantId with names, SKU, attributes, prices, stock, media, description and category hierarchy, cut to enabled fields.
Records are saved with saveObjects into <prefix>.<channel>.<currency>.products, and the variant is deleted from every other channel index so delisted variants disappear.
Algolia failures map to status codes: 413 and an app problem for oversized records, 401 and deactivation for bad credentials, otherwise Algolia's own status.
